facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: IDE assistance and GitHub features vary by plan

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: GitHub's docs say that, starting April 24, 2026, interactions from Copilot Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max—including inputs, outputs, code snippets and associated context—may be used to train and improve models, with a personal opt-out. GitHub says Business and Enterprise customer data is not used for model training under its policy and Data Protection Agreement. This covers training use only; it does not establish the selected model's retention, this account's setting, organization controls or legal suitability.

facts.label: Product self-hosting
facts.value: GitHub describes Copilot cloud agent as an ephemeral development environment powered by GitHub Actions. It defaults to a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner, but a repository setup workflow or organization runner policy can route sessions to a labeled self-hosted Actions runner for access to internal resources. GitHub supports Ubuntu x64 and Windows 64-bit self-hosted runners, recommends ephemeral single-use runners, and says its integrated firewall must be disabled because it is incompatible with self-hosted runners. This changes where agent workspace and commands run; it does not establish local model inference or an offline Copilot service. The organization’s runner policy, firewall and actual session configuration were not inspected.

facts.label: Local model inference
facts.value: GitHub documents client-side Local BYOK for VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and Copilot SDK; the keys are handled client-side and this route removes dependence on the Copilot API. This is separate from Enterprise BYOK, which enterprise owners configure server-side for licensed members and which still uses the Copilot API and internet access. Copilot CLI explicitly supports local Ollama, vLLM and Foundry Local through compatible endpoints. CLI models must support tool calling and streaming; GitHub recommends at least a 128k context window for best results. `COPILOT_OFFLINE=true` prevents the CLI from contacting GitHub, but a remote provider still receives prompts and code context; full isolation requires a provider on the local host or within the same isolated environment. GitHub says Business/Enterprise organization policies can disable Local BYOK in IDEs. These docs establish supported paths, not every feature or a specific account's access/data flow; no model, client or policy was tested.

facts.label: Code / data portability
facts.value: GitHub says Copilot cloud agent works only with GitHub-hosted repositories; its changes are pushed to a branch in the selected repository and can be reviewed as a diff, iterated, and optionally opened as a pull request. Each task is limited to one repository and one branch. This documents a Git-based path for agent-produced code changes, not a general export or migration path for prompts, chat history, session metadata or account settings; those data categories and this account's export controls were not verified. No repository or session migration was tested.

facts.label: MCP support
facts.value: Copilot Chat documents MCP servers for IDE use; GitHub lists VS Code 1.99+ as a prerequisite and requires organization policy enablement for Business or Enterprise members.

sections.heading: Evaluate in the real organization
paragraphs: Trial the same editors and repository permissions used by the team. Confirm whether policy is set by an organization or by an individual account. Compare the features actually enabled for that account rather than a combined marketing feature list.

sections.heading: Count adoption overhead
paragraphs: A trial should include onboarding a second developer, reviewing their changes and revoking access afterward. If preserving the existing workflow is the goal, record how much new configuration the trial introduced.

sections.heading: Check local model and provider boundaries
paragraphs: GitHub documents Local BYOK across several Copilot clients and local Ollama/vLLM use in Copilot CLI. Verify the supported client and organization policy before relying on the path. CLI offline mode blocks GitHub contact, but an external model provider still receives prompts and code context unless it is also local or on-premises.

pros.text: The VS Code documentation covers manual MCP server configuration and installation through the GitHub MCP Registry.
GitHub documents client-side Local BYOK for VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and Copilot SDK; Copilot CLI can connect to local Ollama-compatible endpoints.

cons.text: The documented VS Code setup requires version 1.99 or later.
The MCP servers in Copilot policy is disabled by default and must be enabled for organization or enterprise members on Business or Enterprise plans.

Local BYOK availability depends on the client and organization policy; CLI models need tool-calling and streaming support, and a remote model provider still receives prompts/code context even when Copilot CLI is in offline mode.

faqs.question: What is required for the documented VS Code MCP setup?
faqs.answer: The documentation lists Copilot access and VS Code 1.99 or later. Organization or enterprise members on Business or Enterprise plans also need the MCP servers in Copilot policy enabled.

faqs.question: Does the organization MCP policy govern individual Copilot plans?
faqs.answer: No. GitHub says this policy applies to organization or enterprise users on Business or Enterprise plans, not Copilot Free, Pro, Pro+, or Max.

faqs.question: Can GitHub Copilot use locally run models?
faqs.answer: GitHub lists Local BYOK for VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode, Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and Copilot SDK. Copilot CLI specifically supports local Ollama, vLLM and Foundry Local endpoints; its models must support tool calling and streaming. CLI offline mode prevents contact with GitHub, but a remote provider still receives prompts and code context. Organization policy can disable Local BYOK in IDEs for Business/Enterprise users. Confirm the client and policy; no account or model was tested.

faqs.question: Can GitHub Copilot cloud agent run on a self-hosted runner?
faqs.answer: Yes. GitHub documents ephemeral GitHub-hosted Actions runners by default and an option to use self-hosted Ubuntu x64 or Windows 64-bit runners through setup and organization settings. GitHub recommends ephemeral, single-use runners and requires disabling Copilot's integrated firewall for this configuration. Runner placement does not mean the model runs locally; no organization setting or session was inspected.

faqs.question: How are Copilot cloud-agent code changes returned?
faqs.answer: GitHub says Copilot cloud agent pushes code changes to a branch in the selected GitHub repository; you can review the diff, iterate, and optionally create a pull request. Each task is limited to one repository and one branch. This documents a Git-based code path, not export or migration for prompts, chat history, session metadata or account settings. No repository or session migration was tested.

verdict: Start here if changing the team workflow is a larger cost than changing the assistant. Check seat policies before buying individual subscriptions.
bestFor: Teams evaluating assistance within an established development workflow
notFor: Buyers assuming every feature is available on every plan
migration: Inventory organization policies and supported editor features before switching. Preserve repository instructions outside any one assistant.
gaps: Verify the exact Copilot plan, personal training opt-out and organization or enterprise privacy policies for the account under review; no account settings were inspected.

Review model-specific hosting and retention terms plus the applicable Data Protection Agreement for the enabled models and intended repositories; the published training-use policy is not a complete retention or legal assessment.
Confirm the selected Copilot client, organization Local BYOK policy, model compatibility and provider route; no account, policy, model or inference path was tested.
Confirm the organization's Copilot cloud-agent runner policy, repository override permission, firewall configuration and approved ephemeral runner; no organization setting or runner was inspected.

The reviewed docs establish a Git-based cloud-agent code-change workflow, not export or migration for prompts, chat history, session metadata or account settings; confirm the required export scope. No repository or session migration was tested.
